newsitem.title: GERMANY: Isarescu-RNB not planning to tap markets this year.
newsitem.headline: Isarescu-RNB not planning to tap markets this year.

text.p: The Romanian National Bank said on Wednesday that it had no plans to tap international capital market for funds this year.

Speaking to Reuters at a roadshow in Frankfurt to launch Romania's first mark-denominated eurobond, Mugur Constantin Isarescu, the central bank governor, said it was not necessary for the bank to raise extra funds through debt issuance.
"We already decided that all the borrowings in the name for the Republic of Romania will be done by the finance ministry," Isarescu said.
Asked if central bank itself planned to go to the market this year, he said: "That will not be necessary. We will build up reserves through other means."
He said this would include purchasing from foreign exchange markets, which he said were now "very liquid".
Isarescu also said he expected the central bank's foreign reserves to almost double from their current $1.6 billion level by the end of 1997.
"A level of $3.0 billion in international foreign exchange reserves of the National Bank of Romania is really achievable by the end of the year," Isarescu said.
